newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Austria c.bank's Liebscher sees EMU on time.
newsitem.headline: Austria c.bank's Liebscher sees EMU on time.

text.p: Austrian National Bank president Klaus Liebscher said on Tuesday he was certain that Europe's planned single currency would start on time and that Austria would be among the first members.

"Despite all the gloomy predictions, I have no doubt that the single currency will come into effect on January 1, 1999 as planned. The political will and the necessary dynamic are in place," Liebscher said in a speech to the Swiss chamber of commerce, released in advance in Vienna.
Speculation about a delay was "pointless and risky", Liebscher said.

"Talk of a postponement or a departure from the convergence criteria could have a negative effect on the convergence efforts of individual countries and undermine the confidence of the markets," he continued.

Austria was already well placed to qualify for the single currency, with a low inflation rate, a stable currency and a cost-cutting budget that should steer the budget deficit within three percent of GDP by the end of 1997.
"Austria is well on the way to belonging to the founding members of the single currency," Liebscher said.
Privatisation revenues and restructuring sould help the government trim the debt ratio to below 70 percent of GDP, he added. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
